method: Azure-proposed narrow corrections inspected by Codex before application; acceptance requires a fresh separate review.

patches.old:
As I sat at home, I praised the Lord for everything I had seen. I thought about the commandments: they are good and powerful, they bring joy, they are glorious, and they can save a person’s soul. I said to myself, “I will be blessed if I follow these commandments, and everyone who follows them will be blessed.”

While I was thinking about these things, I suddenly saw him sitting beside me. He said, “Why are you wavering about the commandments I gave you? They are good. Do not waver at all. Instead, clothe yourself with faith in the Lord, and you will follow them, for I will give you strength to do so.”

These commandments help those who are ready to repent[a]. But if they do not live by them, their repentance is useless.

So, you who are turning away from your sins, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down. Clothe yourselves with every righteous virtue. Then you will be able to obey these commandments and stop adding to your sins. If you add no more sins, you will leave your former sins behind. Walk in these commandments of mine—follow them—and you will live as people devoted to God. I have told you these things.

After he had finished speaking with me, he said, “Let us go out into the countryside, and I will show you the shepherds who tend the sheep.”

“Let us go, sir,” I replied.

We came to a plain, where he showed me a young shepherd. The young man was wearing a saffron-colored garment with a varied design.

He was tending a very large flock of sheep. The sheep seemed to be living luxuriously and extravagantly. They were happy and leaped here and there. The shepherd was delighted with his flock. He looked extremely happy, and he ran about among the sheep.

patches.reason: Addresses the three findings independently against the supplied Greek. (1) The commandments and exhortation continue the figure’s speech through ταῦτα [πάντα] παρ' ἐμοῦ λελάληται ὑμῖν; keeping the quotation open, with continuation marks, restores that attribution. (2) ζήσεσθε τῷ Θεῷ promises life in relation to God; 'you will live for God' retains the life assertion rather than replacing it with a characterization of devoted conduct. (3) Reconsideration of the prior clothing rendering: σύνθεσιν ἱματίων denotes an ensemble of clothing, represented by 'outfit'; τῷ χρώματι κροκώδη supplies its saffron color, not a varied design. Existing paragraph divisions, repentance terminology, note marker and note are preserved.
